events.line: A gale kept every boat on the quay and the day's catch with it.
A squall came up out of nowhere. You lost the day's catch, never the boat.
A shoal of mackerel came through so thick the skipper reckoned you could walk across it.
A seal helped itself to the best of the catch and looked entirely unrepentant.
Day trippers paid for a trip round the bay and left a tip, mostly in fudge.
The engine coughed twice and quit. Half a day's fishing with the oars and a lot of language.
A coach of Captain Cook enthusiasts wanted a boat to photograph. You were the prettiest.

upgrades.name: Bigger nets and a second hand
upgrades.text: A bigger haul, and a wage to pay whether the fish come or not.

upgrades.name: An ice hold and a cold store
upgrades.text: The catch arrives fresher, and a rough week costs you less.

upgrades.name: A permanent berth by the quay
upgrades.text: No more circling for a space. Harbour dues, though.

asks.title: Anglers want a day out
asks.text: A party of anglers on the quay has asked whether {deed} would take them out for the day, and whether the boat is, in the circumstances, clean.

options.label: Run a proper charter and wash the deck first
options.say: A good day out, five bass, a story that gets bigger every time it is told.

options.label: Take them out on your normal rounds
options.say: They watch you work and pay for the privilege. The fish are less impressed.

options.label: Say the tide is against you
options.say: It is not. They find another boat.
